resources.string: A Dynamic Island for your punch-hole, over every app.
Island is live over every app
Turn on to place the island over your home screen and apps
Required. This is what lets the island draw on top of everything else.
Optional but recommended. Without it the island only reacts to charging, ringer and headphones.
Android requires an ongoing notification for a service that runs indefinitely.
Drag the needle to set the ceiling. The green band inside it is what the app is really using, measured — not the ceiling echoed back.

The island needs about 30–45 MB and stays there. The ceiling is a limit, not a target: raising it does not make anything faster, and the app will not grow to fill it. Earlier versions allocated real memory to meet the number on the dial, which was waste — that is gone. The reserve for Android is never touched.
The full sandbox: every alert and activity, both cutout shapes, driven by hand.
Unavailable while the theme is running. The demonstration is a separate WebView process worth roughly 80 MB, and running both at once wastes it.
Bring the island back automatically after a restart.
Ongoing notice while the island overlay is active.

On — the island stays as a circle around your camera, even with nothing to show.
Off — with nothing to show, the island collapses into your camera hole and the overlay is removed entirely.
Let the app keep its own footprint down and release cached artwork as it goes.
Everything is on by default. Switch off anything you would rather it stayed quiet about.
Apps the island has heard from. Switch one off and it will never reach the cutout again.
